findings.reason: Using the bounded history view as the final send or link admission check can reject an authorized reply to an older message with a known exact ID, even though the page boundary establishes neither absence nor lack of access and a bounded exact-ID lookup could verify both identity and permission without delegating either to model judgment.

findings.standard: An Instar Agent Is Always a Multi-Machine Entity
findings.reason: The compatibility plan accepts a replica that retains the base message but loses which original it answered, leaving that machine unable to recover a committed part of the conversation when it is the only survivor, with no Pending receipt or repair-before-serving requirement.

Opening a link to an already identified message can require the reader to press Keep looking across history pages, making the reader drive a lookup the application already has the conversation and message IDs to perform.

The opening leads with an internal handoff identifier and assumes the reader knows what “Chief” and “Apple” mean before explaining what a person can do with messages today and what Reply and Copy Link will change.

fit.reason: Readable quote previews and clear unavailable states support operator-surface quality, but the design primarily governs message identity, authorization, and link accuracy and leaves action placement and phone-width usability unspecified.
